title: Barlow Twins: Self-Supervised Learning via Redundancy Reduction
layout_note: An input box X on the left forks into two horizontal branches (Y^A top, Y^B bottom), each running through an encoder trapezoid and a projector trapezoid to an embedding box Z; both branches converge on a grey-scale cross-correlation matrix on the right, which is compared with a double-headed arrow to an identity matrix at the far right.
grouping: No containers or tints. The two branches are stacked lanes with identical shapes; a curly brace under the top branch labelled f_theta groups encoder and projector, and the 'Encoder'/'Projector' names sit under the bottom branch as column labels shared by both.
shapes_depth: Flat. Data (X, Y^A, Y^B, Z^A, Z^B) are white square-cornered boxes with thin black outlines and italic math labels; the encoder is a light-blue narrowing trapezoid and the projector a smaller widening trapezoid, both flat with a thin outline. The two matrices are drawn as pixel grids: one in random greys with a dark diagonal, the target as black diagonal cells on white.
proposed_highlight: The objective is the visual destination: two drawn matrices (empirical cross-correlation C and target identity I) at the right end, joined by a double arrow labelled L_BT, are the only non-box, non-trapezoid elements; a dashed curved arrow from the encoder-projector junction points up to a 'Representations (for transfer tasks)' label.
lesson: Draw the loss as a picture of its target: render the computed cross-correlation as a noisy grey grid and the target as a clean identity grid side by side, linked by a double arrow carrying the loss symbol.
notes: Venue from the first page ('Proceedings of the 38th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 139, 2021').

arrangement.units: Two unframed horizontal lanes (branch A above, branch B below) separated by whitespace, sharing one input box at the left and one matrix comparison at the right.
arrangement.inputs_as: a white box labelled X (no photo); the two distortions are boxes Y^A, Y^B reached by arrows labelled T ~ calligraphic T
arrangement.losses_at: right end, after both lanes converge: matrix C, then a double arrow labelled L_BT, then target matrix I
arrangement.shared: the shared network is drawn once per lane as identical blue trapezoids; a single brace f_theta under the top lane names it

taxonomy.note: training 'other': redundancy-reduction objective that drives the cross-correlation matrix of two views' embeddings to the identity

core.what: two identical horizontal branches (A above, B below) converge on one drawn grey-scale cross-correlation matrix C at the right, which faces a clean identity matrix I across a double-headed L_BT arrow

relations.form: Z^A and Z^B arrows converge diagonally on the noisy grey matrix C, and C is joined to the black-diagonal target matrix I by a double arrow labelled L_BT, the loss drawn as its target

two unframed lanes of the same shapes - distorted-image box Y, encoder trapezoid, projector trapezoid, embedding box Z - stacked top and bottom, a brace under the top lane naming the shared weights f_theta
input box X at the left forks by two diagonal arrows labelled T ~ calligraphic T into Y^A and Y^B, and each lane runs straight left to right
the objective acts on the feature-by-feature correlation matrix, drawn as a small grid of grey cells with a 'feature dimension' double arrow under it

channels.colour: pale blue = trainable network parts (encoder and projector trapezoids); grey levels in C = correlation strength, black in I = target ones; one meaning each
channels.shape: widening/narrowing trapezoids = encoder and projector, white boxes = data and embeddings, cell grids = matrices
channels.line: solid arrows = data flow; double-headed arrow = the loss comparison; dashed curved arrow = 'Representations (for transfer tasks)' pointer
channels.frame: no frames; lanes are separated by whitespace

quality.strengths: the objective is drawn as a picture of what it compares - an empirical correlation matrix beside its identity target - so the core idea reads in 5 s without text; the twin lanes are identical shapes stacked, showing symmetry by geometry; the transfer representation is pointed at the encoder-projector junction rather than drawn as an extra box; short straight paths
quality.weaknesses: inputs and distorted views are white boxes with letters instead of images; the shared weights f_theta are a brace under the top lane only, so weight sharing with the bottom lane is stated in text rather than drawn

insights.structure: One input box forks into two stacked lanes, each data box -> blue encoder trapezoid -> smaller projector trapezoid -> embedding box, and both lanes meet at a cross-correlation grid followed by an identity grid at the far right.
insights.data: Images and embeddings are white outlined boxes with math symbols only (X, Y^A, Z^A), while the cross-correlation is drawn as an actual grey-level grid and the target as a black-diagonal grid, with 'feature dimension' marked by a double arrow under C.
insights.emphasis: The two matrices are the only picture-like elements and sit at the end of the reading path, joined by an L_BT double arrow, so the loss is the visual punchline.
insights.flow: Left-to-right: diagonal arrows fan out from X to the two lanes, run straight through the trapezoids, then converge diagonally into C; a dashed curved arrow rises from between encoder and projector to the 'Representations' label above.
insights.avoid: The labels 'Encoder' and 'Projector' sit only under the bottom lane while f_theta's brace sits under the top lane, so the naming is split across two places.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
